question: Why are community health screening programs so important for managing diabetes in Nigeria?

options.A: Many individuals have undiagnosed diabetes and only discover it when complications arise
options.B: Community outreach prevents all forms of genetic Type 1 diabetes
options.C: Public testing eliminates the need for personal blood glucose meters
options.D: Screening programs replace the need for prescription medications entirely

explanation: Lots of people walk around with high blood sugar without knowing it. Community screenings help catch it early before severe damage happens. That's true public health nursing! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h7)

question: An older adult is crying and terrified about surgery tomorrow. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Allowing a family member to stay close and offering a calm presence
options.B: Leaving the patient alone so they can sort out their thoughts
options.C: Insisting that the patient goes to sleep immediately without talking
options.D: Telling them that surgery is completely risk-free

explanation: Spot on! Having a loved one nearby and knowing a caring nurse is right there brings huge emotional comfort. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h6)

question: What determines when a wrapped sterile instrument pack officially expires and needs re-sterilization?

options.A: The exact number of days marked on the calendar
options.B: Damage, wetness, or a tear in the packaging barrier
options.C: Whether the autoclave machine was washed this week
options.D: The brand name of the paper wrap used by the hospital

explanation: Sterility is event-related; packs stay sterile indefinitely unless the protective packaging is compromised by moisture, dirt, or physical damage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)

question: If a nurse is explaining a new handwashing study to a local community group, how should they share the message?

options.A: Present detailed statistical p-values and regression analyses
options.B: Provide dense theoretical frameworks for academic peer review
options.C: Use clear, jargon-free health education explaining personal wellbeing
options.D: Focus strictly on hospital budget allocations and administrative policy

explanation: Well done! Everyday patients and community members need simple, practical information without any heavy academic terms. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T1#GNS224_U4_T1_h2)

question: What is the main job of the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS)?

options.A: To act as communication lines linking the body to the CNS
options.B: To process and integrate complex memories
options.C: To produce cerebrospinal fluid for the brain
options.D: To directly control hormonal release in the pituitary gland

explanation: The PNS acts like telephone wires, carrying messages back and forth between your body and the central control unit. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h2)

question: An infant receives protective antibodies through breast milk. What type of immunity is this?

options.A: Natural active immunity
options.B: Artificial passive immunity
options.C: Artificial active immunity
options.D: Natural passive immunity

explanation: This is natural passive immunity because the mother's antibodies pass naturally to the baby to give temporary protection. [learn more](GST114_U4_T5#GST114_U4_T5_h7)

question: What is expected of a nurse operating under emergency laws or Good Samaritan rules during a disaster?

options.A: To perform complex surgical procedures outside their normal training
options.B: To act in good faith and stay within their training and scope of practice
options.C: To prioritize personal safety above all community rescue operations
options.D: To completely disregard documentation and patient safety guidelines

explanation: Emergency laws protect you when you help out, as long as you do your best and stay within what you've been trained to do as a nurse. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T6#GNS315_U1_T6_h8)

question: Why do we place a newborn straight onto the mum's bare chest right after birth?

options.A: To promote thermal regulation and early bonding
options.B: To prevent the baby from crying loudly
options.C: To speed up the delivery of the placenta
options.D: To measure the birth weight accurately

explanation: Skin-to-skin contact uses mum's body warmth to keep the baby cozy while helping them bond and start breastfeeding early. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h8)

question: Who takes the lead in providing support at Tier 2 of the MHPSS pyramid?

options.A: Neurosurgeons and clinical pharmacologists
options.B: Community members, family networks, and local leaders
options.C: Only certified trauma therapists
options.D: International psychiatric researchers

explanation: You got it! Tier 2 relies heavily on everyday people—family, friends, and community leaders—helping each other cope through social connection. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T5#GNS314_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why do many patients with chronic kidney disease end up developing anemia?

options.A: The spleen removes healthy blood cells prematurely
options.B: The body destroys red blood cells too quickly
options.C: Dietary iron is no longer absorbed in the gut
options.D: Damaged kidneys fail to produce enough erythropoietin

explanation: You're learning fast! Since sick kidneys can't make enough EPO, the bone marrow doesn't get the signal to build new red blood cells, leading to anemia. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h2)

question: How often should you check vital signs and uterine firmness right after a high-risk delivery?

options.A: Every fifteen minutes for the first hour
options.B: Only when the patient complains of severe pain
options.C: Once a week before scheduled discharge
options.D: Once every twenty-four hours without exception

explanation: That first hour after birth is the highest risk window for sudden bleeding, so we check on mum every 15 minutes to make sure she's stable. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T004#GNS226_U4_T004_h7)

question: What should be a nurse's main focus when giving diet advice to a low-income family?

options.A: Advising them to eat only once every two days
options.B: Recommending affordable, locally available foods
options.C: Telling them to stop eating traditional family meals
options.D: Insisting they purchase expensive imported vitamins

explanation: Good nutrition advice has to be practical. Always recommend foods that the family can easily find and afford in their local market. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T19#GNS214_U1_T19_h7)

question: A patient falls and injures their ankle. Which region of the body is affected?

options.A: Cervical region
options.B: Lower limb
options.C: Axial region
options.D: Thoracic region

explanation: The ankle is part of the lower limb, which falls under the appendicular division of the body. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h3)

question: When is the best time to clean and disinfect a clinical weighing scale?

options.A: Only when visibly soiled with body fluids
options.B: After every single patient use
options.C: Once every week during routine cleaning
options.D: Only at the end of the work shift

explanation: Wiping the scale after each patient prevents the spread of skin infections and germs. Excellent infection control practice! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h7)

question: Why is the skin considered part of the body's primary defense system?

options.A: It produces white blood cells continuously
options.B: It digests harmful toxins entering the body
options.C: It blocks pathogens, chemicals, and physical injury
options.D: It pumps blood to destroy foreign bacteria

explanation: The skin acts as an unbroken physical barrier that stops germs and harsh environmental elements from entering internal tissues. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h1)

question: A family has leftover cooked rice and vegetables. What is the best way to handle them?

options.A: Throw them in the bin immediately to avoid food poisoning
options.B: Refrigerate them promptly and transform them into a fried rice dish
options.C: Feed them exclusively to house pets instead of humans
options.D: Leave them on the kitchen counter overnight for breakfast

explanation: Exactly! Cooling leftovers quickly and repurposing them prevents waste and turns yesterday's food into a brand-new meal. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T004#GNS227_U3_T004_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of doing a colonoscopy?

options.A: Viewing the entire colon lining and removing polyps
options.B: Flushing out impacted stool from the small intestine
options.C: Measuring the exact pressure inside the stomach
options.D: Checking liver enzymes through a small tissue sample

explanation: Well done! A colonoscopy allows the doctor to use a tiny camera scope to look directly at the large bowel lining, take tissue samples, or safely remove growths. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T9#GNS213_U3_T9_h2)

question: Why must nurses check for other physical symptoms alongside pain during a palliative assessment?

options.A: Multiple symptoms interact and can make each other worse, like breathlessness causing panic
options.B: Non-pain symptoms are usually much more dangerous than actual physical pain
options.C: Insurance companies only pay for care if three symptoms are treated at once
options.D: Doctors only look at pain scores and ignore all other bodily complaints

explanation: Symptoms don't happen in isolation. Struggling to breathe can trigger panic, so we need to look at the whole picture! [learn more](GNS321_U4_T4#GNS321_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which leadership style involves sharing decisions and encouraging team input?

options.A: Directive leadership
options.B: Autocratic leadership
options.C: Laissez-faire leadership
options.D: Democratic leadership

explanation: Spot on! Democratic leaders value everyone's voice and love collaborative decision-making on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h4)

question: Why do we calculate children's drug doses based on their body weight?

options.A: Kids can't swallow adult pills
options.B: Hospital insurance requires it for kids
options.C: Children process and clear drugs differently based on size
options.D: It helps check expiration dates

explanation: Children's bodies and organs are still developing, so weight-based dosing is vital to avoid accidental overdose. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T23#GNS122_U1_T23_h7)

question: You accidentally give a patient twice the right dose of their blood pressure medication. What is your very first step?

options.A: Blame the pharmacy assistant for supplying the wrong concentration of tablets.
options.B: Quietly monitor the patient from afar so no one finds out about the mistake.
options.C: Leave the shift early so you are not around when the patient's blood pressure drops.
options.D: Assess the patient's vital signs, notify the doctor, and document the event factually.

explanation: Brave and correct! Patient safety always comes first. Check on your patient, call the doctor immediately, and be honest in your reporting. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T13#GNS125_U2_T13_h6)

question: Why can nystatin oral liquid be used safely for mouth thrush without causing major body-wide side effects?

options.A: It is completely neutralized by normal saliva enzymes
options.B: It is poorly absorbed from the digestive tract into the blood
options.C: It breaks down instantly upon touching the oral mucosa
options.D: It only targets bacterial cell walls instead of human cells

explanation: Spot on! Nystatin stays right where it is needed in the mouth or gut. Because very little enters the bloodstream, whole-body side effects are rare. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T3#GNS215_U6_T3_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing a gastric lavage on a patient?

options.A: To measure daily digestive enzyme production in the pancreas
options.B: To provide long-term nutritional support for unconscious patients
options.C: To relieve chronic constipation by clearing the lower bowels
options.D: To remove ingested poisons from the stomach before they are absorbed

explanation: Gastric lavage acts as an emergency washing technique specifically targeted at flushing out harmful substances from the upper gastrointestinal tract before systemic absorption takes place. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T12#GNS212_U1_T12_h1)

question: What does a patient's viral load test actually measure?

options.A: The exact percentage of body fat lost to lipodystrophy
options.B: The total number of remaining functional white blood cells
options.C: The total functional capacity of the patient's liver
options.D: The amount of active virus circulating in the blood

explanation: Viral load tells us how much of the virus is present in the bloodstream, showing how actively it is multiplying. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h7)

question: Why don't petechiae and purpura turn white when you press your finger on them?

options.A: Blood has leaked entirely outside the blood vessels into the tissue
options.B: The underlying capillaries are permanently dilated from heat
options.C: The skin has become too thick from chronic scratching
options.D: There is an overproduction of clear serum inside the blister

explanation: Since the red blood cells have escaped right out into the skin tissue, pressing on top won't make the color go away. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T8#GNS213_U5_T8_h4)

question: What is the medical term for uncoordinated, clumsy muscle movements caused by a problem in the cerebellum?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Anosognosia
options.C: Ataxia
options.D: Aphasia

explanation: Ataxia simply means a lack of smooth muscle coordination, resulting in those jerky, unsteady movements we see in cerebellar issues. You're learning core clinical terms like a pro! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T22#GNS211_U3_T22_h4)

question: A village has cases of both common colds and severe childhood malnutrition. Which problem should nurses tackle first?

options.A: Neither, because nurses should wait for the rainy season to pass
options.B: Both equally, because all health complaints carry the exact same weight
options.C: Malnutrition, because it has a much higher risk of permanent harm and death
options.D: Common colds, because they affect every single person in the village

explanation: Great choice! We always prioritize life-threatening and severe conditions like malnutrition over mild illnesses that clear up on their own. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T1#GNS124_U3_T1_h7)

question: What type of medication is commonly given to help patients get rid of extra fluid?

options.A: Antibiotics
options.B: Diuretics
options.C: Analgesics
options.D: Anticoagulants

explanation: You nailed it! Diuretics (often called 'water pills') prompt the kidneys to flush out extra salt and water. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T7#GNS123_U3_T7_h7)

question: A patient with a deep pressure ulcer is admitted to your ward. Why is increasing their protein intake so important for their care?

options.A: To cure any underlying bacterial pneumonia
options.B: To support collagen synthesis and tissue repair
options.C: To lower their overall daily caloric intake
options.D: To prevent the development of high blood pressure

explanation: Wounds need raw materials to close up. Protein provides the building blocks (amino acids) needed to grow new skin and heal tissue. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T003#GNS227_U6_T003_h3)

question: What is the most common way people first catch Lassa fever?

options.A: Being bitten by infected mosquitoes at dusk
options.B: Swimming in slow-moving rural rivers
options.C: Eating food contaminated by rat urine or faeces
options.D: Inhaling dust from sweeping dry sandy floors

explanation: Ingesting food or water touched by infected rodent waste is the number one way the virus enters the human body. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T8#GNS214_U1_T8_h3)

question: Which type of measure checks if the specific steps of a new plan are actually being carried out on the ward?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Outcome measure
options.C: Financial measure
options.D: Balancing measure

explanation: You're doing great! Process measures help us check whether we are consistently doing the actual tasks we planned to do. [learn more](GST319_U3_T1#GST319_U3_T1_h4)

question: A patient says they take a blood pressure pill every morning. What crucial detail is still missing?

options.A: The name of the pharmacy that sold it
options.B: The color of the box the pills come in
options.C: The exact dosage strength of the pill
options.D: The weather on the day they started it

explanation: Knowing the drug name is good, but without the specific dose, you cannot assess safety or give correct care. You are thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h3)

question: What does a testable hypothesis need to have?

options.A: Approval from hospital administrators
options.B: Complex mathematical equations and proofs
options.C: Absolute proof that an intervention works
options.D: Variables that can be measured and observed

explanation: If you can't measure it in real life, you can't test it! A good hypothesis always uses observable things. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T10#GNS217_U3_T10_h2)

question: A patient with persistent asthma is prescribed a daily inhaler that works for 12 hours. What drug class is this?

options.A: Short-acting anticholinergics
options.B: Short-Acting Beta-Agonists
options.C: Long-Acting Beta-Agonists
options.D: Inhaled corticosteroids

explanation: That's a Long-Acting Beta-Agonist (LABA)! While SABAs are for quick rescue, LABAs provide steady, long-lasting control throughout the day. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h3)

question: Which of the following best describes osteoporosis?

options.A: Rapid overgrowth of bone in the spinal column
options.B: Sudden accumulation of uric acid crystals in joints
options.C: Decreased bone mass and fragile bone tissue
options.D: Severe inflammation of the synovial joint lining

explanation: Osteoporosis makes bones porous and fragile, like a honeycomb with too many holes, increasing the risk of breaks. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T24#GNS222_U1_T24_h3)

question: A nursing student is asked to run a school mental health drama club. What is the main benefit of using drama for teenagers?

options.A: It guarantees that none of the students will ever feel sad
options.B: It tests their ability to memorize medical textbooks word for word
options.C: It replaces the need for professional psychiatric nurses
options.D: It entertains them while teaching healthy ways to cope with emotional stress

explanation: Creative methods like drama engage young minds effectively, making sensitive health messages relatable and easy to remember. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h7)

question: Why must raw meat always go on the lowest shelf of the fridge?

options.A: So it is faster for the cooks to grab
options.B: To keep it closest to the fridge cooling fan
options.C: To stop meat juices from dripping onto other foods below
options.D: Because raw meat likes warmer spots than veggies

explanation: Gravity is sneaky! If raw meat drips onto ready-to-eat foods below it, it spreads harmful germs. Always keep raw meat at the bottom. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T006#GNS227_U7_T006_h5)

question: Why must instrument box locks and ratchets be kept open during the sterilization process?

options.A: To make it easier to count them after the cycle
options.B: To allow steam to reach all hidden surfaces
options.C: To make the instrument tray look neat and tidy
options.D: To prevent the metal handles from melting

explanation: Keeping hinges and box locks open ensures that the sterilizing steam makes full contact with every part of the metal. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T9#GNS123_U5_T9_h8)

question: What happens to the body during activation of the sympathetic nervous system?

options.A: Digestion speeds up to process recent meals
options.B: Heart rate increases and airways dilate for quick action
options.C: Pupils constrict to focus on close objects
options.D: Blood flow is directed entirely to the stomach

explanation: The sympathetic division prepares the body for stressful or emergency situations by boosting alertness and physical readiness. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T1#GNS222_U3_T1_h4)

question: Who are some of the best local partners for community health nurses working to prevent FGM?

options.A: Religious leaders, school teachers, and women's groups
options.B: International lawyers and foreign embassy officials only
options.C: Private security guards and military personnel exclusively
options.D: Traditional cutters and commercial blade suppliers

explanation: Correct! Teaming up with respected community voices helps nurses reach families effectively and spread the message against FGM. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T5#GNS225_U6_T5_h7)

question: What is the main reason we tell postpartum mothers to drink plenty of fluids and eat high-fiber foods?

options.A: To stop painful uterine afterpains
options.B: To turn lochia serosa into lochia rubra
options.C: To shrink the size of the bladder
options.D: To prevent postpartum constipation

explanation: Straining after delivery can be very painful, especially with stitches or piles (hemorrhoids). Fluids and fiber keep things soft and easy! [learn more](GNS226_U1_T010#GNS226_U1_T010_h5)

question: How is a multidisciplinary care plan different from a plan made by just one health worker?

options.A: It removes the need for nursing assessments completely
options.B: It allows the patient to change medical diagnoses at any time
options.C: It combines insights from various fields into one unified set of goals
options.D: It focuses exclusively on hospital discharge procedures

explanation: You're doing great! A team plan blends nursing, social work, and medical insights so every angle of the patient's health is covered. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h5)

question: Which of these is a mineral-based drug commonly used to neutralize stomach acid?

options.A: Penicillin G
options.B: Morphine sulfate
options.C: Digoxin extract
options.D: Calcium carbonate

explanation: Calcium carbonate is a mineral compound often found in over-the-counter antacids to quickly soothe heartburn. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why must diet care in Nigeria make use of local staples like garri, beans, and yams?

options.A: Because local staples contain zero carbohydrates and cannot raise blood sugar
options.B: To make sure the meal advice is affordable, practical, and fits the patient's culture
options.C: Because imported foreign foods are illegal to prescribe in government hospitals
options.D: To prevent the Ministry of Health from auditing the hospital kitchen

explanation: Patients find it much easier to stick to meal plans when they use foods they already know, buy, and love eating every day. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T001#GNS227_U4_T001_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to review and update diet plans from time to time?

options.A: Because patients get bored eating the same foods for more than three days
options.B: Because hospital regulations require rewriting charts weekly
options.C: Because food items change their vitamin content every single month
options.D: Because client needs, health status, and life circumstances change over time

explanation: Life isn't static, and neither is health! Regular checks ensure the diet plan keeps up with the patient's changing body and life. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T014#GNS227_U4_T014_h7)

question: What is the main purpose of priority setting in community mobilisation?

options.A: To make sure every single disease is treated on day one
options.B: To delay health interventions until funding runs out
options.C: To let health workers choose projects without community input
options.D: To focus resources on the most urgent health problem first

explanation: Since resources are limited, ranking problems helps the community tackle the most critical issue first. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h5)

question: When is the best time to check the second set of vital signs after starting a blood transfusion?

options.A: After thirty minutes
options.B: At the very end of the bag
options.C: After two hours
options.D: After fifteen minutes

explanation: The 15-minute mark is crucial because most serious acute reactions happen right at the beginning of the infusion. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T18#GNS122_U1_T18_h6)

question: Why is the needle directed just over the top of the lower rib during insertion?

options.A: To make sure the needle reaches the lowest point of the diaphragm
options.B: To avoid injuring the nerves and blood vessels running under the ribs
options.C: To prevent the fluid from leaking out onto the patient's skin
options.D: To allow the doctor to see the needle clearly without an ultrasound

explanation: Blood vessels and nerves travel right beneath the ribs, so inserting the needle just above the lower rib protects these structures. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T17#GNS221_U2_T17_h3)

question: Why does obstetric fistula often cause women to face social isolation in their communities?

options.A: Patients lose their ability to speak after the injury
options.B: Continuous incontinence leads to severe social stigma and shame
options.C: Government laws require isolation of all surgical patients
options.D: Traditional healers forbid them from leaving their homes

explanation: Because of constant leaking of urine or stool, affected women often face heartbreaking stigma and misunderstanding from their communities. As nurses, our empathy and care are crucial in supporting and healing them. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the root cause behind most cases of coronary artery disease?

options.A: Infection of the heart valves by bacteria
options.B: Weakening of the heart muscle walls
options.C: Atherosclerosis from fatty plaque buildup
options.D: Enlargement of the right atrium

explanation: Spot on! Cholesterol and fats slowly accumulate inside the arteries over time, narrowing the pathway and making it hard for blood to pass through. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T10#GNS111_U2_T10_h4)

question: Even if a woman has received the HPV vaccine, why must she still go for regular cervical cancer screening later in life?

options.A: The vaccines do not protect against all high-risk strains of HPV
options.B: Screening tests are required to check if the vaccine was absorbed
options.C: Vaccinated individuals have a higher risk of developing infections
options.D: The vaccine wears off completely after exactly five years

explanation: Spot on! While the vaccine defends against the most common cancer-causing HPV strains, other less common high-risk strains can still cause issues, making regular screening still necessary. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T10#GNS313_U3_T10_h9)

question: Which IEC channel works best for reaching a scattered rural population quickly?

options.A: One-on-one clinic counseling
options.B: Detailed written pamphlets
options.C: Radio broadcasts
options.D: Individual home visits

explanation: Correct! Radio is a powerful tool because it travels far and wide, reaching people in remote areas in no time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h4)

question: What major mistake should you avoid when collecting a swab sample?

options.A: Using a transport tube that is completely clear of liquid
options.B: Parting the labia majora gently with the non-dominant hand
options.C: Touching the surrounding skin and contaminating the swab
options.D: Rotating the swab against the surface of the lesion too long

explanation: Be careful! Touching normal skin introduces random bacteria that can mess up the test and hide the real cause of the infection. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h4)

question: What happens to a drug revolving fund over time if free drugs are given out but never paid for by a subsidy?

options.A: The pharmacy inventory will steadily deplete and collapse
options.B: The government will automatically double its funding
options.C: The fund will grow larger and more profitable
options.D: Drug manufacturers will begin supplying free items forever

explanation: Remember, a revolving fund depends on money returning when drugs are sold. If stock is given away without a replacement fund, the pharmacy will soon run out of cash to restock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary relationship between a patient's health status and their nutrition?

options.A: Dietary intake only affects surgical patients and nobody else.
options.B: Illness and nutrition have a direct, two-way effect on each other.
options.C: Health status has no real impact on how the body uses food.
options.D: Nutrition only matters after a patient has completely recovered.

explanation: Health status and nutrition influence each other constantly; sickness changes how the body handles nutrients, while poor nutrition worsens illness. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h1)

question: What is a major challenge when using wearable health devices in some Nigerian communities?

options.A: Excessive availability of high-speed fiber optic cables
options.B: Strict government bans on all digital wristwatches
options.C: A complete lack of patients suffering from chronic illnesses
options.D: Unstable electricity supply and limited internet connectivity

explanation: Frequent power cuts and poor network signals can sometimes make it tough to keep live health data syncing smoothly. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T11#GNS212_U4_T11_h6)

question: How is Type 2 diabetes different from Type 1 diabetes?

options.A: Type 2 requires immediate lifelong oral medication without dietary changes
options.B: Type 2 is strictly an acute condition that resolves without long-term treatment
options.C: Type 2 only affects elderly patients who have a family history of kidney disease
options.D: Type 2 involves insulin resistance and relative deficiency rather than total destruction

explanation: In Type 2 diabetes, your body still makes insulin, but your cells resist using it properly—unlike Type 1 where the beta cells are completely wiped out. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h2)

question: A patient has a large ovarian cyst and complains of a dull ache and needing to pee very often. Why is she experiencing frequent urination?

options.A: Her kidneys are producing extra urine due to stress
options.B: The cyst is pressing against her urinary bladder
options.C: The infection from the cyst has spread to her kidneys
options.D: Her hormone levels are causing her to drink more water

explanation: It's all about anatomy! A big cyst takes up space in the pelvis and pushes right against the bladder, making her feel the urge to go more often. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h3)

question: What is a key safety requirement for storing cleaning chemicals in a day care centre?

options.A: Storing them securely out of reach of children
options.B: Placing them next to food preparation counters
options.C: Keeping them unlocked on low shelves for easy access
options.D: Mixing them with drinking water for cleaning

explanation: Toxic chemicals must always be stored securely away from children to prevent accidental poisoning or chemical burns. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why does a patient moving around during a digital blood pressure check often cause an error?

options.D: Movement creates false pressure bumps that confuse the machine's computer

question: Which low-cost test is commonly used in Nigerian primary health clinics to check for early cervical cell changes?

options.C: Positron emission tomography scans
options.D: Magnetic resonance imaging scans

question: When drawing an ogive, where do we place the class boundaries?

question: What is usually the very first physical sign of puberty in girls?

options.A: Onset of the first menstrual period

question: What is the medical term used when a stitched wound unexpectedly pops open?

options.B: Cellulitis
options.C: Hematoma
options.D: Necrosis

explanation: When a wound separates or pops open, we call it dehiscence. It usually happens if there's too much tension or movement before the tissue heals. You're learning pro terminology! [learn more](GNS311_U4_T2#GNS311_U4_T2_h7)

question: When public health nurses talk about 'community structure', what are they mostly looking at?

options.A: The financial budget of the local government
options.B: How people are organized and how power is distributed
options.C: The physical blueprint of houses in a neighborhood
options.D: The exact number of hospital beds in a local clinic

explanation: Think of community structure as the backbone of the neighborhood: who holds influence, how groups connect, and how leadership works. Spotting this helps you know who to talk to when you want to start a health project! [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h1)

question: What procedure is often needed if leftover placental tissue is causing ongoing postpartum sepsis?

options.A: Total abdominal hysterectomy
options.B: Appendectomy
options.C: Evacuation of the uterus
options.D: Bilateral tubal ligation

question: How does the lower esophageal sphincter help protect you from GERD (heartburn)?

options.A: It acts like a muscular valve that stops stomach acid from flowing upward

options.C: It secretes thick mucus to coat the top of the stomach

explanation: The lower esophageal sphincter is your body's one-way valve. It stays tightly closed and only opens to let food travel down into the stomach. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T10#GNS213_U3_T10_h2)

question: What does the abbreviation HAI stand for in nursing practice?

options.A: High acuity illness
options.B: Hygiene assessment indicator
options.C: Healthcare-associated infection
options.D: Hospital antiseptic index

explanation: HAIs are infections patients acquire while receiving medical treatment in a hospital or clinic facility. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h8)

question: A patient scheduled for discharge on home IV antibiotics says they want to stop the medicine early because the pain is gone. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Suggest waiting until the next scheduled clinic visit in three months
options.B: Tell the patient to double their pill dose to make up for the missed days
options.C: Explain that stopping early can cause the infection to return stronger and harder to treat
options.D: Agree and instruct the patient to take over-the-counter pain pills instead

explanation: Patients must finish their entire course of antibiotics to ensure all bacteria are eradicated, preventing a relapse of chronic osteomyelitis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h9)

question: Which statement best describes informed consent in a longitudinal study?

options.A: It is an ongoing process that may need to be renewed as the study progresses
options.B: It is completely optional if the participants are hospital nurses
options.C: It is a one-time signature that never needs to be discussed again
options.D: It is only required on the very last day of data collection

question: What is the primary advantage of using an ultrasound for genitourinary assessment?

options.B: It provides a biopsy of the kidney tissue automatically
options.C: It does not expose the patient to radiation
options.D: It measures blood pressure inside the renal arteries

explanation: Ultrasound relies on sound waves rather than ionizing radiation, making it a safe diagnostic imaging option. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why do scientists create semi-synthetic versions of natural antibiotics like penicillin?

options.A: To help it survive stomach acid and fight a wider range of germs
options.B: To ensure the medication can only be given via painful injection
options.C: To completely destroy all antibacterial properties of the drug
options.D: To make the manufacturing process slower and more expensive

explanation: Tweaking natural molecules helps create stronger antibiotics that can survive stomach acid and beat tougher germs. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T5#GNS125_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why do community health nurses keep a close eye on people living in the same house as a leprosy patient?

options.B: They are at higher risk because they spend so much time together
options.C: They are legally banned from leaving the house during treatment
options.D: They must swallow preventive antibiotics for years

question: What is a confounding variable?

options.B: An outside factor related to both exposure and disease
options.C: The main exposure being studied by the nurse
options.D: A deliberate intervention created by the research team

explanation: Think of a confounder as a sneaky third factor that messes with our results by hiding the true relationship between our exposure and disease. [learn more](GST114_U2_T19#GST114_U2_T19_h5)

question: When should you definitely NOT perform a rectal washout?

question: What type of leadership style involves inviting input from team members before making decisions?

options.D: Autocratic leadership

question: Why is it important to write down any learning barriers (like poor eyesight or hearing) in the nursing notes?

options.B: It allows the hospital to charge extra fees for communication
options.C: It guides incoming nurses on how to adapt future teaching sessions
options.D: It proves the patient was difficult and uncooperative

explanation: Documenting barriers helps the whole nursing team communicate effectively without making the patient repeat themselves. Excellent teamwork! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h8)

question: Why do modern syringe drivers have security locks on their control panels?

options.A: To prevent the battery from falling out during transport

question: What is the main class of medications used first-line to treat common intestinal roundworms?

question: A patient insists that their mother, who passed away years ago, is coming to visit today. What is the best nursing action?

options.B: Scold the family members for not correcting the patient's false memory
options.C: Ignore the comment completely and pretend you did not hear anything
options.D: Acknowledge the feeling behind the statement and gently redirect their attention

question: A nursing mum wants steady, long-lasting energy for her daily chores. What should you recommend she eat?

options.A: Pure cooking oils taken directly by the spoonful
options.B: Salt-free butter eaten in large morning portions
options.C: Simple refined sugars found in carbonated beverages
options.D: Complex carbohydrates like yams and whole grains

question: Which health history is a strict warning (contraindication) against using estrogen-based birth control?

question: What is a common misconception people have about children with conduct disorders?

question: What is the main medication given during Active Management of the Third Stage of Labour (AMTSL)?

question: Why is a rectovaginal fistula often psychologically distressing for a patient?

question: Which of these bacterial airborne illnesses is still a major health concern across Nigeria?

question: How can community leaders help improve low immunization uptake in rural areas?

question: Why are functional emergency referral systems so important for pregnant women in rural Nigerian communities?

question: Why are health programs more successful when the community helps design them?

question: What triggers the cephalic phase of digestion?

question: Which action shows a nursing manager applying great leadership on a busy ward?

question: Why do we ask the patient to empty their bladder right before the PET scan machine starts?

question: A patient walks into the clinic with lower tummy pain and unusual discharge. What serious upper-body complication should a nurse watch out for if this is left untreated?

question: Why is it so important to keep raw meat away from ready-to-eat foods in the kitchen?

question: How do learning disabilities differ from global developmental delays?

question: What is the primary definition of ambulation in healthcare?

question: What temperature must a standard freezer maintain to keep food safe?

question: Which type of transmission happens when tiny germ particles float in the air over long distances?

question: Why is hypertension frequently called the 'silent killer'?

question: A community nurse needs official guidelines to start a new polio vaccine drive. Where is the best place to check first?

question: Why should a nurse avoid rushing a patient during a bed-to-wheelchair transfer?

question: What is the best way for a nurse to find out about a newly admitted patient's usual sleeping habits?

question: What do we call the layer of a membrane that is stuck directly onto the surface of an organ?

question: Which sign is a major red flag for a developing perineal hematoma after delivery?

question: What is a major fear that stops many patients from sharing their HIV status with family?

question: Why is keeping patient information strictly confidential so vital in HIV nursing care?

question: What is the main dietary focus when caring for a patient with high blood pressure (hypertension)?

question: What is the main reason the brain undergoes structural changes during pregnancy?

question: A patient complains of constant dizziness and trouble keeping their balance. Which part of the ear is likely involved?

question: Where are the kidneys located in the human body?

question: What is the primary and most potent estrogen produced by the ovaries during female puberty?

question: What is a primary responsibility of community health nurses regarding food security?

question: Why is the skin considered a window into a patient's general health status?

question: Why is simple health information alone often insufficient to change community habits?

question: When we classify joints by their 'function', what are we actually looking at?

options.C: How much movement the joint allows

question: Why do sulfonylurea drugs carry a higher risk of causing low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) compared to Metformin?

options.A: They destroy counter-regulatory hormones like glucagon and cortisol
options.B: They force the kidneys to dump excess sugar into the urine too quickly
options.C: They actively stimulate insulin release from the pancreas regardless of blood sugar levels
options.D: They completely block the liver from releasing any stored glucose ever

explanation: Spot on! Sulfonylureas keep pushing the pancreas to pump out insulin even if blood sugar levels are already dropping, which can cause hypoglycaemia. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h4)

question: What term describes the swallowing difficulties caused by muscle weakness in degenerative disorders?

options.A: Apraxia
options.B: Aphasia
options.C: Dysarthria
options.D: Dysphagia

explanation: Dysphagia is the medical term for difficulty swallowing—something we must watch out for closely to prevent food or liquid from entering the airway. You're doing awesome! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h6)

question: Why is reuniting families so important right after a disaster strikes?

options.A: It replaces the need for any medical triage assessments.
options.B: It helps restore the survivor's sense of safety and emotional control.
options.C: It guarantees the patient will never develop any physical illnesses.
options.D: It reduces the administrative burden on hospital billing departments.

explanation: Spot on! Finding loved ones helps chip away at the terrible isolation and panic that comes with a traumatic event, helping survivors feel secure again. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is a normal, expected reaction shortly after getting a shot?

options.A: Sudden loss of consciousness lasting over one hour
options.B: Instant swelling of the tongue and throat airways
options.C: Mild soreness and swelling at the injection site
options.D: Widespread blistering rash across the entire body

explanation: A little bit of pain, swelling, or low fever just means the body's immune system is hard at work building protection! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T73#GNS214_U1_T73_h7)

question: Why do hospitals love using modular theatres with integrated digital control panels?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any nurses inside the room
options.B: To reduce the cost of electricity used by surgical lights
options.C: To allow patients to watch movies during local anesthesia
options.D: To streamline equipment controls and improve communication efficiency

explanation: Brilliant! Having gas outlets, lights, and communication tools in one central smart hub makes everything run much smoother during a busy case. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h3)

question: Why did military nursing groups become so important during the Crusades?

options.A: To translate ancient Greek philosophy texts
options.B: To provide organized shelter and treat wounded soldiers
options.C: To manufacture advanced gunpowder and tactical weapons
options.D: To govern newly conquered political territories

explanation: During the Crusades, special nursing groups were needed to set up safe resting places and care for fighters and travelers who got hurt. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is one of the main ways nurses advocate for reproductive rights in everyday practice?

options.A: Financially sponsoring family planning clinics out of their own salaries
options.B: Providing non-judgmental, confidential care and education to all patients
options.C: Refusing to treat patients who disagree with hospital policies
options.D: Changing national health laws through Supreme Court litigation

explanation: As a bedside nurse, your best advocacy tool is treating every patient with respect, keeping their secrets safe, and educating them without any personal bias. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before encouraging a patient to take high-dose supplements?

options.A: To find out if the patient is allergic to plastic medicine bottles
options.B: To make sure the patient can afford the expensive brand names sold in pharmacies
options.C: To calculate the exact hospital bed tax for nutritional therapy
options.D: To confirm the specific nutrient deficiency rather than guessing based on general fatigue

explanation: We test to be sure what's actually lacking. Guessing can lead to wasting money or even vitamin toxicity! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T014#GNS227_U7_T014_h4)

question: Why do babies born to teenage mothers face higher risks of developmental delays?

options.A: Complete absence of breast milk production in teenagers
options.B: Mandatory separation of mother and child at birth
options.C: A combination of physical prematurity and the mother's limited caregiving maturity
options.D: Automatic genetic mutations caused by young maternal age

explanation: You got it! Being born early plays a part, and young mothers may also need extra guidance on caring for a baby as they grow. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T8#GNS312_U3_T8_h5)

question: A mum comes to the clinic having tummy tightening. When she walks around, the contractions stop completely and her cervix is still tightly closed. What's happening?

options.A: Rupture of membranes
options.B: Onset of the second stage
options.C: False labour contractions
options.D: Active phase true labour

explanation: These are false labour (or Braxton Hicks) contractions! True labour contractions keep getting stronger even if the mum moves around. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T002#GNS226_U3_T002_h2)

question: What is the big benefit of using a head-to-toe approach for a physical exam?

options.A: It requires the patient to change positions constantly
options.B: It allows the nurse to finish the examination in under two minutes
options.C: It eliminates the need to inspect the skin
options.D: It ensures a structured and thorough assessment without missing body parts

explanation: Going head-to-toe builds a solid routine. It makes sure you never accidentally skip checking an important body system! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T3#GNS124_U6_T3_h6)

question: A patient is complaining of terrible menstrual cramps. Which chemical messenger is mostly to blame for these strong uterine contractions?

options.A: Thyroxine
options.B: Cortisol
options.C: Insulin
options.D: Prostaglandins

explanation: Blame the prostaglandins! When the endometrium releases these chemicals, they make the uterine muscles squeeze tightly, causing those painful cramps (dysmenorrhea). [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h6)

question: How is primordial prevention different from primary prevention?

options.A: Primordial prevention relies entirely on medications, while primary relies on surgery
options.B: Primordial prevention is only used for infectious diseases, while primary is for chronic illnesses
options.C: Primordial prevention targets broad social and environmental policies, while primary targets specific health habits
options.D: Primordial prevention happens after a disease is diagnosed, while primary happens before

explanation: Think of primordial prevention as tackling big-picture societal conditions, while primary prevention focuses on personal habits and exposures like vaccines. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T91#GNS214_U1_T91_h2)

question: Which task best shows a staff nurse directly participating in quality assurance?

options.A: Reporting a faulty intravenous pump before it harms a patient
options.B: Complaining about low salary during a shift handover
options.C: Refusing to help clean a patient after an accident
options.D: Leaving ward charts blank until the end of the week

explanation: Brilliant! Spotting a broken tool and speaking up before it hurts a patient is the textbook definition of proactive quality assurance in action. [learn more](GST319_U4_T1#GST319_U4_T1_h5)

question: During early cleavage (cell division), what happens to the overall size of the cell mass?

options.A: It shrinks drastically because cells lose their water content
options.B: It grows rapidly in size as each cell feeds and expands
options.C: It flattens out into a sheet of tissue inside the tube
options.D: It stays roughly the same while cell numbers increase

explanation: Even though the cells are multiplying rapidly, they all stay snug inside the original protective shell (zona pellucida) so the total size remains similar at first. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h4)

question: A patient had a right-sided mastectomy last year. Which arm should you use for venepuncture?

options.A: On the right arm
options.B: On the left arm
options.C: In the right hand veins only
options.D: Either arm without preference

explanation: Always avoid the arm on the side of a previous mastectomy because lymph flow there is compromised, making infections much harder to fight off. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why is advocacy so important in primary health care, way beyond just giving treatments?

options.A: It directly cures infectious diseases without medication
options.B: It guarantees immediate government funding for hospitals
options.C: It replaces the need for community health workers
options.D: It addresses systemic barriers that limit healthcare access

explanation: Great thinking! Handing out medications doesn't fix big problems like poverty or bad roads to the clinic. Advocacy tackles those root barriers that keep people from getting care. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T7#GNS124_U4_T7_h1)

question: Which processing method destroys all microorganisms, including bacterial spores?

options.A: Cleaning
options.B: Sterilization
options.C: Disinfection
options.D: Sanitization

explanation: Sterilization is the only process that completely eliminates every form of microbial life, including highly resistant bacterial spores. [learn more](GST114_U2_T12#GST114_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the main goal of using the 'teach-back' method after educating a patient?

options.A: To fulfill a legal requirement for signing surgical consent forms
options.B: To allow the nurse to take a break while the patient teaches the class
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory for academic medical trivia
options.D: To have the patient explain instructions in their own words to verify understanding

explanation: Teach-back isn't testing the patient—it's testing *us*. If they can explain it back easily, you know your teaching hit the mark! [learn more](GNS215_U4_T6#GNS215_U4_T6_h7)

question: How can a new home care agency best protect its nurses from safety risks when visiting unfamiliar areas?

options.A: Instructing nurses to never document any clinical findings
options.B: Stopping all home visits after morning hours
options.C: Vetting client locations and utilizing tracking or communication tools
options.D: Requiring families to purchase expensive hospital equipment

explanation: Brilliant! Checking locations beforehand and using check-in tools helps keep field nurses safe and secure. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T9#GNS324_U1_T9_h7)

question: What was the old theory of 'spontaneous generation' all about?

options.A: Microorganisms mutate rapidly when exposed to sunlight
options.B: Living creatures can form directly from nonliving matter
options.C: Pathogens multiply only inside the human bloodstream
options.D: All living cells come exclusively from preexisting living cells

explanation: People used to believe that living things like maggots or mice could just pop up out of nowhere from mud or trash. Science proved them wrong! [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h2)

question: A patient says, 'My BP is normal today, so I'll stop my drugs.' What is the best way for a nurse to reply?

options.A: Suggest replacing the prescribed drugs with local palm wine
options.B: Agree that normal readings mean the disease has gone away permanently
options.C: Tell the patient to double the dose whenever they feel dizzy
options.D: Explain that the medication controls the condition rather than curing it

explanation: Normal readings just mean the medication is doing its job! Stopping it will cause the pressure to shoot right back up. Patient education is key! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h6)

question: Why are malnourished individuals much more vulnerable to severe infections?

options.A: Their immune systems lack the proper nutrients to mount a strong defense
options.B: Pathogens are naturally attracted to low protein levels in the blood
options.C: Stomach acid becomes too weak to kill ingested bacteria
options.D: Malnutrition stops white blood cells from circulating through the veins

explanation: Good nutrition is the fuel for immunity. Without the right nutrients, the body simply doesn't have the building blocks to fight off sickness effectively. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T2#GNS313_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is the main safety benefit of using high-tech simulation manikins in nursing school?

options.A: Students can practice high-risk emergencies without putting real patients in danger
options.B: It removes the need for any supervision by qualified nursing instructors
options.C: It guarantees that every student will pass their final licensing board exam
options.D: It prevents students from ever making a documentation error on the ward

explanation: Simulation gives you a safe playground to make mistakes, learn from them, and master emergencies without risking human lives. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h4)

question: A patient comes to the clinic with a fever and headache, but is fully alert and able to swallow drugs. How do you classify this?

options.A: Asymptomatic malaria
options.B: Chronic malaria
options.C: Severe malaria
options.D: Uncomplicated malaria

question: During a menstrual check-up, which patient symptom is an immediate red flag that needs prompt clinical attention?

options.A: Soaking through a sanitary pad every hour for several hours in a row
options.B: Mild abdominal cramping on the first day of the period
options.C: A cycle length that varies by two days each month
options.D: Mild breast tenderness a week before menstruation begins

explanation: Soaking a pad every single hour for hours on end is never normal—it's a serious sign of heavy bleeding and potential hemorrhage that needs immediate help. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T4#GNS121_U5_T4_h7)

question: What jelly-like structure in the inner ear gets pushed when moving fluid hits it during a head turn?

options.A: Otolith
options.B: Cupula
options.C: Tectorial membrane
options.D: Macula

explanation: The cupula acts just like a tiny swinging door inside your ear, moving whenever the fluid pushes against it. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T8#GNS211_U4_T8_h3)

question: Which of these is a very common skin sign of an adverse drug reaction?

options.A: High fever with muscle stiffness
options.B: Yellow discoloration of the urine
options.C: Hives and generalized skin itching
options.D: Sudden swelling of the knee joints

explanation: Spotting rashes, hives (urticaria), and itchy skin is often the first visible clue that a patient is reacting badly to a drug. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h3)

question: Why can high hospital examination tables be tough for patients with mobility challenges?

options.A: They increase the financial cost of routine blood tests
options.B: They prevent patients with mobility limitations from transferring easily
options.C: They take up too much space in standard nursing stations
options.D: They make it difficult for doctors to hear heart sounds clearly

explanation: Think about a wheelchair user trying to climb up! Fixed high furniture can block access and make simple checks really difficult without proper equipment. You're learning fast! [learn more](GNS225_U5_T15#GNS225_U5_T15_h1)

question: What is a major health risk in overcrowded refugee or displaced persons (IDP) camps?

options.A: A sudden surplus of safe drinking water
options.B: Complete elimination of nutritional deficiencies
options.C: Immediate eradication of chronic lifestyle illnesses
options.D: Rapid outbreaks of waterborne and communicable diseases

question: Where should used injection needles and sharp blades be discarded?

options.A: Puncture-proof sharps containers

options.C: Open cardboard boxes near sinks
options.D: Standard black plastic waste bins

question: What is the main goal of grouping drugs into pharmacological classes?

options.A: To determine the exact retail cost of prescription drugs
options.B: To establish the legal expiration date for various drug classes
options.C: To identify which pharmaceutical company manufactured the medicine
options.D: To group medications based on their mechanism and physiological effects

explanation: Grouping drugs by how they work in the body helps you easily predict their actions and safety profiles without memorizing every single pill! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h1)

question: What is the key difference between inherited and acquired bleeding disorders?

options.C: Inherited disorders develop later in life from poor diet.
options.D: Acquired disorders never involve platelet abnormalities.

question: What is the job of the jelly-like substance (colloid) found inside your thyroid gland?

options.C: To store thyroid hormone precursors until they are ready for release
options.D: To produce calcitonin for the regulation of blood calcium levels

question: A nurse notices that two different injectable drugs have very similar label designs and are stored right next to each other. What is the best immediate risk reduction action?

options.B: Wait until a medication error actually happens before telling anyone

question: Why is it clinically necessary to evaluate the male partner during infertility workups?

question: How does a public health nurse help prevent abuse by starting a support group for young, first-time parents?

options.C: By monitoring parents for illegal drug use in their homes
options.D: By building parenting skills and reducing social isolation

question: Why must IV fluids be given carefully to a trauma patient with low blood pressure and suspected heart injury?

question: What is the primary focus of a strategic plan in nursing management?

options.A: Immediate treatment of a single patient

question: Why should you connect a health topic to the daily life experiences of adult learners?

options.A: Ministry regulations state that lectures must last for at least two hours

options.C: Older individuals cannot memorize new information without a story

question: What kind of air pressure is kept inside the operating room to keep outside air from rushing in?

question: In a research study, what is the independent variable?

options.B: The patient outcome being measured

question: What severe long-term complication can happen when a baby's head presses against soft tissues for too long during obstructed labour?

question: A manager wants to check if nurses are consistently signing off on medication times. Which tool is best for this?

options.A: Staff annual performance reviews

options.D: Nursing chart audits

question: Why is personal safety planning so important for home health nurses?

options.D: Hospital security guards accompany them on every single visit

question: Why is giving people only cheap, starchy food not enough for long-term health?

options.C: It is always more expensive than fresh vegetables
options.D: It does not prevent micronutrient deficiencies or hidden hunger

question: How do school health programs help keep female students in class?

options.A: By strictly punishing any student who fails a monthly health examination
options.B: By managing hygiene, health screenings, and offering a safe support system
options.C: By providing free uniforms, books, and daily hot meals for all students
options.D: By taking over classroom teaching responsibilities from regular teachers

explanation: Correct! Providing clean facilities, health checks, and a listening ear helps girls feel safe, healthy, and confident to stay in school. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T47#GNS214_U1_T47_h5)

question: Why are graphs and visual charts so helpful for busy nurses?

options.C: They replace all written patient progress notes in the medical record
options.D: They are legally required by hospital management for promotion

question: What is the main advantage of using a relative frequency column instead of just raw counts?

question: Which of these is a major reason for internal displacement, especially in Northern Nigeria?

question: What does drug over-prescription mean in clinical practice?

options.A: Storing too many pharmaceutical products in the hospital pharmacy

options.D: Failing to give any medication to a critically ill patient

question: What is the main job of thermoreceptors in the skin?

options.D: Converting mechanical vibration into electrical signals

question: Why must nurses weave therapy principles into everyday nursing care?

options.B: To shorten the length of the patient's hospital stay
options.C: To replace the physical therapist entirely during night shifts
options.D: To reduce the number of medical documents in the chart

explanation: You got it! Consistency helps patients rebuild their neural pathways and physical strength much faster when practiced all day long. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T5#GNS225_U2_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of leadership theories in nursing?

options.A: Strictly enforcing hospital parking rules for night shifts
options.B: Explaining how individuals influence others to achieve goals
options.C: Eliminating the need for written nursing care plans
options.D: Determining the exact salary scale for hospital administrators

explanation: Leadership theories simply help us understand how leaders guide, motivate, and work together with teams to reach common goals in healthcare. You've got this! [learn more](GST321_U3_T2#GST321_U3_T2_h1)

question: How do major health authorities view the medicalisation of FGM?

options.A: As a helpful stepping stone toward total eradication
options.B: As an acceptable compromise for cultural preservation
options.C: As a severe violation of human rights and medical ethics
options.D: As a minor disciplinary issue handled by local clinics

question: What do we call the mismatch when a baby's head is too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?

question: What is the usual maximum flow rate recommended for a standard nasal cannula?

options.D: 6 Liters per minute

question: What is a major danger if a patient suddenly stops taking their long-term degenerative medications without talking to a doctor?

options.A: A sudden, severe return of symptoms or withdrawal
options.B: An immediate boost in liver and kidney function
options.C: Complete regeneration of normal nerve cells
options.D: An instant and permanent cure of the disease

explanation: You got it! Stopping chronic meds cold turkey can send the body into a severe rebound, making symptoms much worse than they were before. Tapering is usually needed! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T19#GNS222_U4_T19_h7)

question: What advice should you give a patient about sex while she is undergoing treatment for an infection?

options.A: Increase sexual frequency to help flush out the remaining bacteria

options.C: Mixed into a large bowl of hot porridge for breakfast
options.D: Directly down the center of the infant's throat

explanation: Smart nursing trick! Pushing liquid into the side of the cheek prevents choking and gagging, making medicine time much calmer for baby and nurse. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T21#GNS122_U1_T21_h6)

question: What does it mean for a nursing research project to show 'originality'?

options.A: Adding fresh insights or applying concepts in a new setting
options.B: Inventing a brand-new hospital building design
options.C: Writing a research paper without using any past references
options.D: Copying successful studies from foreign countries word-for-word

explanation: Well done! Originality means bringing a fresh perspective, new data, or trying an existing idea in a brand-new setting like our local Nigerian hospitals. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T1#GNS217_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why is it so important to screen and care for depression during neuro-rehab?

options.A: Family members do not experience any stress as long as the client feels physically comfortable.
options.B: Unmanaged depression can significantly reduce a client's motivation and willingness to participate in physical therapy.
options.C: Psychological distress is contagious and often spreads quickly among other clients in the ward.
options.D: Emotional symptoms are always temporary and disappear completely without any professional intervention.

explanation: Mind and body are deeply connected! If a patient is silently battling deep depression, they won't have the emotional energy to push through tough therapy sessions. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T22#GNS222_U3_T22_h7)

question: A charge nurse is planning a shift with several very sick patients. What is the safest staffing approach?

options.A: Rotate every nurse to a different room every single hour
options.B: Assign all junior nurses to the most complex patients alone
options.C: Pair experienced nurses with junior staff to ensure safe care
options.D: Keep all senior nurses on one shift and all juniors on another

explanation: You're learning fast! Mixing skill levels protects patients and gives junior nurses fantastic mentorship on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U6_T1#GST321_U6_T1_h3)

question: What is the main way that most foodborne germs get into our bodies?

options.A: Vector-borne transmission
options.B: Fecal-oral route
options.C: Direct sexual contact
options.D: Airborne droplet route

explanation: It sounds unpleasant, but tiny, microscopic traces of waste pathogens find their way onto food or water and enter right through the mouth. Handwashing is our best defense! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h3)

question: In public health nursing, how do we look at a "community"?

options.A: A static collection of buildings and roads managed by local government
options.B: A strict political boundary with no movement of people across borders
options.C: A group of patients admitted to the same hospital ward at one time
options.D: A dynamic social system with interacting individuals sharing common interests

explanation: Think of a community as a living network of people who affect and support each other—not just houses on a map! [learn more](GNS225_U1_T5#GNS225_U1_T5_h1)

question: In which zone of the surgical suite can staff members wear regular street clothes?

options.A: Sterile core zone
options.B: Restricted zone
options.C: Unrestricted zone
options.D: Semi-restricted zone

explanation: The unrestricted zone is the welcome area where you enter before changing into your scrubs. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T3#GNS123_U5_T3_h2)

question: Why are open-ended questions best when taking a drug history?

options.A: They are much faster to document in the nursing notes
options.B: They stop the patient from talking too much
options.C: They encourage the patient to share detailed, honest information
options.D: They prevent the patient from asking about their hospital bill

explanation: Open-ended questions let patients explain their routines in their own words instead of just saying yes or no. Excellent interviewing tip for the wards! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h4)

question: What makes malaria an example of biological vector-borne transmission?

options.A: The mosquito only carries the parasite on the outside of its physical legs
options.B: The malaria parasite develops and multiplies inside the mosquito before being injected
options.C: The malaria pathogen is spread purely through human-to-human coughing
options.D: The disease can only live inside warm-blooded animal reservoirs

explanation: In biological transmission, the parasite undergoes a necessary part of its life cycle inside the vector before it can infect a new host. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the difference between isolation and quarantine?

options.A: Isolation requires chemical disinfection of clothing, whereas quarantine requires surgical operations
options.B: Isolation is used exclusively for vector-borne diseases, while quarantine is for waterborne diseases
options.C: Isolation separates individuals who are already sick, while quarantine restricts healthy people who were exposed
options.D: Isolation is a voluntary home practice, whereas quarantine is ordered by the military

explanation: Easy to remember: Isolation is for the sick ones, quarantine is for healthy contacts who might have caught it. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h6)

question: Which accessory gland makes the biggest chunk of the fluid found in semen?

options.A: Prostate gland
options.B: Seminal vesicles
options.C: Bulbourethral gland
options.D: Cowper's gland

explanation: The seminal vesicles are great providers—they supply the bulk of the fluid volume, including sweet sugars to give the sperm energy. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T2#GNS121_U4_T2_h5)

question: During a routine checkup, a patient mentions mild pain during intercourse that started recently. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Acknowledge the concern non-judgmentally and explore further or refer for screening
options.B: Tell the patient that pain is completely normal and requires no attention
options.C: Advise the patient to stop all intimate activity permanently
options.D: Immediately prescribe strong hormone medications without a doctor's order

explanation: Early screening and open discussion allow nurses to catch issues promptly and guide the patient toward the right care. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h7)
